title: How many children does a row of triangles show?
description: A teacher in Berasia shows how often children slept at least nine hours, with one triangle for ten children. The video reads the key first, then turns each row into a number, while Keeko doubts that five triangles are five children.
teaching_notes: One idea: read the key, then multiply the whole symbols by it, and a half symbol is half of the key. Watch for children who count the triangles as single children.

source: Pictograph with a key of ten: hours of sleep in Berasia
video_script.why: The child reads a key larger than one and handles a half symbol.
video_script.substitution: none: the book's own sleep pictograph
video_script.anchor: {{NAME_9}}'s pictograph of how often children slept at least nine hours
video_script.wrong_move: counts the triangles without reading the key
video_script.payoff_line: Forty children always slept less than nine hours.

final_answer.spoken: fifty children always slept at least nine hours, twenty five sometimes did, and forty always slept less than nine hours

names.{{NAME_9}}: teacher from Berasia who makes the sleep-hours pictograph

maths_rules: Never: 4 triangles, 4 x 10 = 40; never sleeping at least 9 hours means always sleeping less than 9 hours.
video_script.design: A key line, then three rows of triangles labelled always, sometimes and never, with the half triangle in the middle row.

beats.on_screen: title card with three rows of triangles labelled always, sometimes and never, and a half triangle in the middle row

marks.scene: the title card arrives with the three rows
marks.rows: the three rows of triangles light up one after another
marks.ask: a question mark lights up beside the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is an example from your book, made by {{NAME_9}} in Berasia.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Three rows of triangles show how often children slept at least nine hours.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many children does each row of triangles show?

beats.on_screen: the three rows and the question mark stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a card shows one triangle beside the words ten children, and a half triangle beside the words five children; the word key is written above

marks.key: the note one triangle equals ten children is circled and named the key
marks.half: a half triangle appears beside the whole one

narration: <bookmark mark='key'/>The note that tells what one triangle stands for is called the key.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Here, one triangle stands for ten children, so half a triangle stands for five.

beats.on_screen: Given: key 1 triangle = 10 children; Always 5 triangles; Sometimes 2 triangles and a half; Never 4 triangles

marks.given: the key is written as the given
marks.rows: the three rows of triangles are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one triangle stands for ten children.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Always has five triangles, sometimes has two and a half, and never has four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the children who always slept at least 9 hours, who sometimes did, and who always slept less than 9 hours

marks.find: the three lines to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find three counts: always, sometimes, and always less than nine hours.

marks.always: the five triangles of the first row are counted and each is marked as ten

narration: <bookmark mark='always'/>Step one, the row for always has five triangles.
Each triangle is ten children, so five tens make fifty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: Sometimes: 2 whole triangles and a half, 2 × 10 + 5 = 25 children

marks.whole: the two whole triangles are marked as ten each
marks.half: the half triangle is marked as five

narration: <bookmark mark='whole'/>Step two, the row for sometimes has two whole triangles and a half.
Two triangles are twenty children.
<bookmark mark='half'/>Half a triangle is five, and twenty and five make twenty five.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: Never slept 9 hours means always less than 9 hours: 4 triangles, 4 × 10 = 40 children

marks.never: the row for never is read as the children who slept less than nine hours
marks.four: the four triangles are counted as ten each

narration: <bookmark mark='never'/>Step three, the row for never has four triangles.
Never sleeping nine hours means always sleeping less than nine hours.
<bookmark mark='four'/>Four tens make forty.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Fifty children always slept at least nine hours, and twenty five sometimes did.
Forty children always slept less than nine hours.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: the number 5 written beside the always row and crossed out; the key box 1 triangle = 10 children circled; the number 50 replaces it

marks.doubt: the number five appears beside the always row
marks.ten: the number fifty replaces the crossed number

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks five triangles are five children, because there are five triangles.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the key says one triangle stands for ten children.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>We read the key first, and then five triangles show fifty children.
